title: Chapter 34
text: 6 Which, pathetically enough, was true. Colin really had been wanting to learn Sanskrit. It’s sort of the Mount Everest of dead languages. 7 Arabic: “I love you.” 8 It might be helpful to think about this graphically. Colin saw the Dumper/Dumpee dichotomy on a bell curve. The majority of people are lumped somewhere in the middle; i.e., they’re either slight Dumpees or slight Dumpers. But then you have your Katherines and your Colins: 9 Like a smart monkey, Colin possessed an extensive vocabulary, but very little grammar. Also, he didn’t know “dead” was pronounced ded . Forgive him. He was two. 10 Which, for the record, Colin actually named. The others called it “The Stretch,” but then one time when they were about to do it to him, Colin shouted, “Don’t give me an abdominal snowman!” And the name was so clever that it stuck.
